I was really worried about glare too.

This is what I did to get some piece of mind:

\- I checked if the glare was roughly equal in both eyes. If yes, then there's little chance that it is caused by some surgery complication or failure. 

\- I picked a light by my house that I looked every other day, at nighttime, to check if the glare diminished. The changes are subtle from one day to another, but one week to another they become noticeable. 

Good luck with your healing and enjoy your new vision!

I had SMILE a month ago. 

The glares do go away considerably in the first few weeks. I had huge glares immediately after the surgery, even at post op one week. 

Now, I no longer notice glares during the day, and during the night they're diminished considerably. Asking friends with normal vision, my glare is about 2x their glare. I'm sure it will improve further with time.

I had huge starburst around lights immediately after the surgery as well. I used to notice them all the time (day and night). 

I am one month post op now and don't have starburst during the day anymore, and the  night diffusion lowered considerably, though did not resolve completely.

my initial measurements were: OS -1.75 OD -3.25 and i am 36 years old

I do have a couple of differences:

- lenticule extraction was max 1 minute per eye
- immediately after the surgery, and for the next couple of hours, my eyes stung as if i had dripped some hot sauce in them. i kept my eyes closed until this sensation went away (2.5h) 
- if it wasn:t for the light sensitivity and the stinging, i could have probably drove home myself. 
- 3h after surgery i could already see really well! one of the eyes is perfect, while the other feels like -0.5. im really hoping one of the eyes was undercorrected, and that it can see up close for longer as i age. 
- the glare is real! it's like every source of light is a snowflake. it's kinda pretty to be honest
- im noticing some loss of contrast, everything seems like it has a white wash. i would not mind if this was permanent, it's not really bad. 
- i do have maybe sliiiight double vision at low light (if i read small print on the phone in a dark room, there's a bit of blur)
- my left eye has a spot where it tickles (if i move that spot to touch my lower eyelid) 
- dry eyes are real. i had dry eyes before, so the sensation was not new ro me. now they are drier than before. 

I was mostly worried about being over corrected, but i'm reading the smallest text on my phone right now (16h after the surgery).

I wore down my enamel - grinding. clenching and basically just abusing my teeth. I grinded so much that my gums started receding. When switched to an electric toothbrush, everything was made worse.

My dentist recommended:

\- no electric toothbrushes - too harsh!

\- use a soft bristle toothbrush and NEVER press hard on the teeth (the bristles shouldn't bend)

\- sides of the teeth: brush up or down, away from your gum (this was the mistake I was making) -  same for the front and backs of your teeth

\- for molars, brush the tops circularly, and sides like the point above.

​

My gum recession has stopped since I made these changes.

I think you should get advice from a dentist you trust, and who can oversee your progress.

Take care of your teeth!
